column146:
for the logreg I was missing clear result tables in a statistics-sence. Without those tables I have basically no information to really evaluate the model itself and the parameters with their coefficients.
For the ML-Levels I was missing summary statistics on the variables. If some of them are highly correlated, which I assume is the case, I doubt their usefulness to include them. It might even be more beneficial to exclude some variables but I haven't seen outputs which illustrate those kinds of analysis.
column147:
Based on my missing understanding behind the ML-models and their behaviour over time I did see all the output graphs and coefficients, but it did not increase my trust in the model or my understandung on how things work. If the model would come to different conclusions, based on the groups of people I include in the model, this would give me a better idea of how the model runs. Judged by the risk factors, I do see results which are not plausible for me. Taking the example of age: An increasing age results in a lower PD. I assume because of the correlation between age and wealthiness, but the likelihood of death or illness increases, which would decrease the likeliness of paying back credits. It could also result in an increased cost of living, because of medical treatments. 
So, although the number of plots increased, the economic-interpretability stayed on a constant, rather low, level, for my feeling.
